verses.text: Jesus heard the Pharisees had clocked he was making and baptizing more disciples than John.
To be clear, Jesus himself wasn’t baptizing people—his disciples were—
so he dipped out of Judea and headed for Galilee.
He had to pass through Samaria.
He reached a Samaritan town called Sychar, near the land Jacob had handed down to his son Joseph.
Jacob’s well was there. Jesus was worn out from the trip, so he sat down by the well. It was about noon.
A Samaritan woman came to draw water. Jesus asked her, “Could you get me a drink?”
His crew had gone into town to pick up food.
The woman said, “You’re a Jew, and I’m a Samaritan woman. Why are you asking me for a drink?” (Jews didn’t associate with Samaritans.)
Jesus answered, “If you knew what God gives—and who’s asking you for a drink—you’d ask him, and he’d give you living water.”
She said, “Sir, you don’t even have a bucket, and this well is deep. Where would you get this ‘living water’?
Are you greater than our ancestor Jacob, who gave us this well? He drank from it, and so did his kids and livestock?”
Jesus answered, “Everyone who drinks this water will get thirsty again.
But whoever drinks the water I give won’t thirst again—ever. It’ll become a spring inside them, flowing into eternal life.” 💧
The woman said, “Sir, give me that water, so I won’t get thirsty or have to keep making this trek here to draw water.”
Jesus told her, “Go call your husband and come back.”
She answered, “I don’t have a husband.” Jesus said, “That’s right—you don’t have a husband.
You’ve had five husbands, and the man you’re with now isn’t your husband. What you said is true.”
She said, “Sir, I can tell you’re a prophet.
Our ancestors worshiped on this mountain, but you Jews say Jerusalem is the place to worship.”
Jesus told her, “Believe me, the time is coming when you’ll worship the Father neither on this mountain nor in Jerusalem.
You worship what you don’t know; we worship what we know, because salvation comes from the Jews.
But the time is coming—and it’s already here—when true worshipers will worship the Father in spirit and truth. The Father is looking for people like that to worship him.
God is spirit, and the people who worship him must worship in spirit and truth.”
The woman said, “I know the Messiah is coming—the one they call Christ. When he gets here, he’ll explain everything to us.”
Jesus told her, “I am he—the one talking with you.”
Just then, his disciples came back. They were shocked he was talking with a woman, but nobody asked, “What do you want?” or “Why are you talking with her?”
The woman left her water jar, ran back into town, and told the people,
“Come meet a man who told me everything I’ve ever done. Could he be the Christ?”
They streamed out of town and started coming to Jesus.
Meanwhile, the disciples kept urging him, “Rabbi, please eat something.”
But he said, “I have food to eat that you don’t know about.”
The disciples said to each other, “Did someone bring him food?”
Jesus told them, “My food is to do what the one who sent me wants and finish his work.
Don’t you say, ‘Four more months till harvest’? I’m telling you, lift your eyes and check the fields—they’re already ripe for harvest.
The harvester gets paid and gathers a crop for eternal life, so planter and harvester can celebrate together.
So this saying is true: ‘One person plants; another comes along and harvests.’
I sent you to harvest what you didn’t work for. Others did the hard work, and you’ve stepped into their labor.”
Many Samaritans from that town believed in Jesus because of the woman’s report: “He told me everything I’ve done.”
When the Samaritans came to him, they begged him to stay. He stayed with them for two days.
Many more believed because of what he said.
They told the woman, “We believe now, not just because of what you said. We’ve heard him ourselves, and we know he really is the Christ, the Savior of the world.”
After those two days, Jesus left and went to Galilee.
Jesus himself had said that a prophet isn’t honored in his own homeland.
When he arrived in Galilee, the people welcomed him. They’d seen what he did in Jerusalem during the festival, because they’d been there too.
Jesus came back to Cana in Galilee, where he had turned water into wine. A royal official was there whose son was sick in Capernaum.
When the man heard Jesus had come from Judea to Galilee, he went to him and begged him to come down and heal his son, who was at death’s door.
Jesus told him, “Unless you people see signs and wonders, you won’t believe.”
The official said, “Sir, please come down before my child dies.”
Jesus told him, “Go on home. Your son lives.” The man trusted Jesus’ word and headed back.
As he headed down, his servants met him with the news, “Your child lives!”
He asked them when his son had started getting better. They said, “The fever left him yesterday at about one in the afternoon.”
The father realized that was the exact time Jesus had told him, “Your son is alive.” So he and everyone in his household believed.
This was the second sign Jesus did after coming from Judea to Galilee.
